text: In the name of God, the most beneficent, the most merciful.
Honourable UN Secretary General, Mr. Ban Ki-moon, respected President General Assembly,
Honourable UN Envoy for Global Education, Mr. Gordon Brown, respected elders, and my dear brothers and sisters, Asalaamu Alaikum.
Today, it is an honour for me to be speaking again after a long time.
Being here with such honourable people
is a great moment in my life.
And it's an honor for me that today I'm wearing a shawl of Benazir Bhutto Shaheed.
I don't know where to begin my speech.
I don't know what people would be expecting me to say.
But first of all, thank you to God for whom
We all are equal.
And thank you to every person who has prayed for my fast recovery and a new life.
I cannot believe how much love people have shown me.
I have received thousands of good wish cards and gifts from all over the world.
Thank you to all of them.
Thank you
to the children whose innocent words encouraged me.
Thank you to my elders whose prayers strengthened me.
I would like to thank my nurses, doctors, and the staff of the hospitals in Pakistan, in the UK, and the UAE government who have helped me to get better and recover my strength.

I fully support Mr. Ban Ki-moon, the Secretary General, in his Global Education First initiative, and the work of the UN Special Envoy, Mr. Gordon Brown, and the respected President General Assembly, Volk Yaramic.
I thank all of them for their leadership that they continue to give.
They continue to inspire all of us to action.
Dear brothers and sisters, do remember one thing.
Malala Day is not my day.
note: Clarifies the meaning of Malala Day.

text: Today is the day of every woman, every boy and every girl who have raised their voice for their rights.
There are hundreds of human rights activists and social workers who are not only speaking for their rights but who are struggling to achieve their goal of peace, education and equality.
note: Mentions other activists and their struggle.

text: Thousands of people have been killed by the terrorists and millions have been injured.
I am just one of them.
note: States personal connection to the struggle.

text: So here I stand.
So here I stand, one girl among many.
I speak not for myself, but for those without voice can be heard.
note: States her purpose is to speak for others.

text: Those who have fought for their rights.
Their right to live in peace.
note: First item in a list of rights.

text: their right to be treated with dignity, their right to equality of opportunity, their right to be educated.
note: Completion of the list of rights.

text: Dear friends, on the 9th of October 2012, the Taliban shot me on the left side of my forehead.
They shot my friends too.
They thought that the bullet would silence us.
But they failed.
And out of that silence came thousands of voices.
The terrorists thought that they would change my aims and stop my ambitions.
But nothing changed in my life except this.
Weakness, fear and hopelessness died.
note: First part of the contrasting transformation.

text: strength, power, and courage was born.
note: Second part of the contrasting transformation.

text: I am the same Malala.
My ambitions are the same.
note: Second item in list of continuity.

text: My hopes are the same.
note: Third item in list of continuity.

text: And my dreams are the same.
note: Fourth and final item in list of continuity.

text: Dear sisters and brothers, I am not against anyone.
Neither am I here to speak in terms of personal revenge against the Taliban or any other terrorist group.
I am here to speak up for the right of education of every child.
I want education for the sons and daughters of the Taliban and all the terrorists and extremists.
note: Extends education advocacy even to enemies.

text: I do not even hate the Taliban who shot me.
Even if there is a gun in my hand and he stands in front of me, I would not shoot him.
This is the compassion that I have learned from Muhammad, the prophet of mercy, and Jesus Christ and Lord Buddha.
This is the legacy of change that I have inherited from Martin Luther King, Nelson Mandela, and Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
note: Credits historical figures for legacy of change.

text: This is the philosophy of nonviolence that I have learned from Gandhiji, Bacha Khan, and Mother Teresa.
is the forgiveness that I have learned from my father and from my mother.
This is what my soul is telling me.
Be peaceful and love everyone.
Dear sisters and brothers,
we realize the importance of light when we see darkness.
We realize the importance of our voice when we are silenced.
note: Second philosophical observation, relevant to her experience.

text: In the same way, when we were in Swat, the north of Pakistan, we realized the importance of pens and books when we saw the guns.
note: Applies philosophical point to personal experience in Swat.

text: The voice saying,

the pen is mightier than sword was true the extremists were and they are afraid of books and pens the power of education the power of education frightens them they are afraid of women the power of the voice of women frightens them and that is why
note: Explains why extremists are afraid, using repetition.

text: They killed 14 innocent students in the recent attack in Quetta.
note: Example of extremist violence (first item in a list of 'that is why' anaphora).

text: And that is why they killed female teachers and polio workers in Khaywar Pakhtunkhwa.
That is why they are blasting schools every day.
Because they were and they are afraid of change, afraid of equality that we will bring into our society.
note: Explains the underlying fear of extremists.

text: And I remember

that there was a boy in our school who was asked by a journalist why are the taliban against education he answered very simply by pointing to his book he said a talib doesn't know what is written inside this book they think
note: Anecdote about a boy explaining Taliban's stance.

text: that God is a tiny little conservative being who would send girls to the hell just because of going to school.
note: Critiques the Taliban's misinterpretation of religion.

text: The terrorists are misusing the name of Islam and Pashtun society for their own personal benefits.
note: Accuses terrorists of misuse of religion/culture.

text: Pakistan is a peace-loving, democratic country.
Pashtuns want education for their daughters and sons.
And Islam is a religion of peace, humanity and brotherhood.
note: Affirms the true nature of Islam.

text: Islam says it's not only each child's right to get education, rather it's their duty and responsibility.
note: Explains education as an Islamic duty.

text: Honorable Secretary-General, peace is necessary for education.
note: States premise about peace and education.

text: In many parts of the world, especially Pakistan and Afghanistan, terrorism, wars and conflicts stop children to go to their schools.
We are really tired of these wars.
Women and children are suffering in many ways in many parts of the world.
In India, innocent and poor children are victims of child labour.
note: Example of child suffering in India.

text: Many schools have been destroyed in Nigeria.
People in Afghanistan have been affected by the hurdles of extremism for decades.
note: Example of long-term suffering from extremism.

text: Young girls have to do domestic child labour and are forced to get married at early age.
note: Example of forced child labor and marriage.

text: Poverty, ignorance, injustice, racism and the deprivation of basic rights
are the main problem faced by both men and women.
Dear fellows, today I am focusing on women's rights and girls' education because they are suffering the most.
note: Declares focus on women's and girls' rights.

text: There was a time when women social activists asked men to stand up for their rights, but this time we will do it by ourselves.
note: States women's resolve to act for themselves.

text: I'm not telling men to step away from speaking for women's rights.
note: Clarifies her stance on men's role.

text: Rather, I'm focusing on women to be independent, to fight for themselves.
So dear sisters and brothers, now it's time to speak up.
note: Call to action for speaking up.

text: So today, we call upon the world leaders to change their strategic policies in favor of peace and prosperity.
note: Call to leaders for policy change (first item in anaphora list).

text: We call upon the world leaders that all the peace deals must protect women's and children's rights.
note: Call for protection of women's/children's rights in peace deals.

text: A deal that goes against the rights of women is unacceptable.
We call upon all governments
to ensure free compulsory education all over the world for every child.
note: Specifies call for free education for every child.

text: We call upon all the governments to fight against terrorism and violence, to protect children from brutality and harm.
note: Call for fighting terrorism and protecting children.

text: We call upon the developed nations to support the expansion of educational opportunities for girls in the developing world.
note: Call for developed nations to support girls' education.

text: We call upon all the communities to be tolerant.
To reject prejudice based on caste, creed, sect, colour, religion or gender.
note: Lists types of prejudice to reject.

text: To ensure freedom and equality for women.
note: Call for women's freedom and equality.

text: so that they can flourish.
We cannot all succeed when half of us are held back.
note: Argument for universal success requiring equality.

text: We call upon our sisters around the world to be brave, to embrace the strength within themselves and realize their full potential.
note: Call to women for bravery and potential.

text: Dear brothers and sisters, we want schools.
and education for every child's bright future.
We will continue our journey to our destination of peace and education.
No one can stop us.
We will speak up for our rights and we will bring change through our voice.
note: Promise to speak up and bring change.

text: We believe
in the power and the strength of our words.
Our words can change the whole world because we are all together, united for the cause of education.
note: States belief in words' power due to unity.

text: And if we want to achieve our goal, then let us empower ourselves with the weapon of knowledge.
note: Call to use knowledge as a weapon.

text: and let us shield ourselves with unity and togetherness.
note: Call to use unity as a shield.

text: Dear brothers and sisters, we must not forget that millions of people are suffering from poverty, injustice and ignorance.
note: Reminder of global suffering (first item in anaphora list).

text: We must not forget that millions of children are out of their schools.
note: Reminder of children out of school (second item).

text: We must not forget that our sisters and brothers are waiting for a bright, peaceful future.
note: Reminder of the hope for a better future (third item).

text: So let us wage a global struggle against illiteracy, poverty and terrorism.
Let us pick up our books and our pens.
note: Call to use books and pens.

text: They are our most powerful weapons.
note: Declares books and pens as weapons.

text: One child, one teacher, one book and one pen can change the world.
note: Iconic statement on the power of education.

text: Education is the only solution.
note: States education as the sole solution.

text: Education first.
Thank you.
